correctness.rationale: The quantifiers cover every integer \(n\ge2\), marked index \(1\le i\le n\), and real \(\tau\ne0\). Real Jacobi spectral simplicity implies average mixing is a Gram matrix of eigenvector-coordinate squares; Vandermonde and adjugate expansions give the dimension of deleted-minor polynomials. The independent parity sector is a basis of size \(\lceil n/2\rceil\); explicit reflection-difference polynomials reduce the remaining rank to Chebyshev coprime-divisibility. Their gcd is \(U_{\gcd(i,n+1)-1}\), and its bounded parity E-space has exact dimension \(\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor\). The central case is reflection-symmetric. The exact finite checker independently verifies 1014 polynomial identities and 680 matrix ranks for \(2\le n\le18\) and \(\tau\in\{-2,3/2,1,3\}\). These tests corroborate the fully general proof and do not establish it by enumeration.

value.rationale: The path is a canonical finite one-dimensional quantum transport model, and a marked-site energy is a standard local perturbation. The theorem is a complete sharp rank classification across all path sizes and real nonzero defect strengths, with a surprising \(\gcd(i,n+1)\)-indexed resonance and a centered odd-path obstruction. The exact full-rank design criterion directly informs how one local potential can remove or fail to remove symmetry-induced null modes in long-time mixing. This is not a routine unmarked-path rank restatement or an arbitrary finite table.
